dicas.texto: Você está indo bem! Se o denominador de uma fração indica em quantas partes dividimos o inteiro, o que o número 12 na fração 4/12 nos diz sobre a segunda reta?
Tente dividir a segunda reta numérica em 12 partes iguais. Use o campo 'numline2_noLabel_denom' para definir esse número e veja como a reta se ajusta.
Agora que a reta está dividida em 12 partes, conte 4 desses pequenos espaços a partir do zero para marcar o ponto.
Ao marcar o ponto na quarta marcação de 12, ele fica exatamente alinhado com o ponto 1/3 da reta de cima? Se sim, eles representam a mesma distância!

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; pergunta exibida "Are they the same? Correct the equal sign."; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 1, uma acima da outra: na Linha 1 a fração dada já está marcada pelo tutor; na Linha 2 o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividir (campo de denominador + confirmar) e marca o ponto da fração equivalente; à direita das retas, a igualdade entre as duas frações é mostrada em caixas: as da esquerda vêm preenchidas e, na da direita, o aluno digita o NUMERADOR (o denominador alvo já aparece); há também um seletor de comparação ("≟", "=", "≠") entre as duas frações; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir a Linha 2, marcar o ponto, digitar o numerador, comparar, concluir).

dicas.texto: What does the denominator tell you about the number line?
Look at the denominator of the fraction represented on Line 2 and use it to determine the number of equal intervals.
The target fraction is written with twelve equal parts in the whole.
Divide the interval from 0 to 1 into as many equal sections as the denominator of 4/..., then submit that count.
Which part of a fraction tells how many equal sections make the whole?
Read the denominator of the target fraction and enter that number in the denominator field.
The denominator in the target fraction is the number shown below the fraction bar.
Enter the target denominator in the field, then press the confirmation control to divide Line 2.
What does the numerator tell you to count on a number line?
Start at 0 and count equal intervals toward 1 using the numerator as the number of intervals.
Use the twelve divisions you created and count from 0 toward the point represented by the numerator.
Move right one equal interval at a time until you have counted the numerator's number of intervals, then mark that point.
Which number tells how many equal parts are selected?
Count the intervals from 0 to the marked point and use that count as the numerator.
The denominator is already shown as twelve; enter the number of selected intervals.
Count the intervals between 0 and the marked point, then type that count into the numerator field.
What should the comparison sign show when two fractions represent the same amount?
Compare the marked positions on Line 1 and Line 2 before choosing the sign.
The two marked points coincide between 0 and 1.
Because the marked points are identical, choose the sign that means the two quantities have the same value.
What should you check before submitting an equivalence problem?
Review the marked points, the numerator field, and the comparison sign.
Make sure both number lines show the same location and the equality statement is complete.
When every part of the equivalence statement is confirmed, use the completion button to submit the problem.

hints.message: What does the numerator tell you to count on a number line?
Start at 0 and count equal intervals toward 1 using the numerator as the number of intervals.
Use the twelve divisions you created and count from 0 toward the point represented by the numerator.
Move right one equal interval at a time until you have counted the numerator's number of intervals, then mark that point.

misconceptions.description: Aluno ignora a relação de equivalência e foca na diferença entre os numeradores
misconceptions.feedback: Different numerators do not automatically mean different amounts. Compare the positions on the number lines after marking the fractions.

misconceptions.description: Aluno confunde a posição do numerador e denominador
misconceptions.feedback: You reversed the fraction. The numerator counts the selected intervals, while the denominator counts all equal intervals.

nodes.description: Enter the numerator of the equivalent fraction in the right-hand numerator box.
nodes.instruction: Enter the numerator of the equivalent fraction in the right-hand numerator box.

hints.message: Which number tells how many equal parts are selected?
Count the intervals from 0 to the marked point and use that count as the numerator.
The denominator is already shown as twelve; enter the number of selected intervals.
Count the intervals between 0 and the marked point, then type that count into the numerator field.

misconceptions.description: Aluno confunde a posição do numerador e denominador
misconceptions.feedback: You treated the denominator as the numerator. The numerator is the number of selected parts, while twelve is the total number of parts.

nodes.description: Select the comparison sign that shows the two fractions have the same value.
nodes.instruction: Select the comparison sign that shows the two fractions have the same value.

hints.message: What should the comparison sign show when two fractions represent the same amount?
Compare the marked positions on Line 1 and Line 2 before choosing the sign.
The two marked points coincide between 0 and 1.
Because the marked points are identical, choose the sign that means the two quantities have the same value.

nodes.description: Click Done to finish after confirming the fraction equivalence.
nodes.instruction: Click Done to finish after confirming the fraction equivalence.

hints.message: What should you check before submitting an equivalence problem?
Review the marked points, the numerator field, and the comparison sign.
Make sure both number lines show the same location and the equality statement is complete.
When every part of the equivalence statement is confirmed, use the completion button to submit the problem.
